title: Strong correlations and local self-energies from on-site ensembles
authors: Alberto Carta, Hugo U. R. Strand, Michael Schüler, Nicola Marzari
abstract: Addressing the many-body electronic-structure problem is a central goal of modern condensed-matter physics. Paramagnetic Mott insulators, in particular, have long represented a challenge for standard approaches, such as density-functional theory. Historically, these systems have been tackled either by considering many-body dynamics, as in the case of dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), or, more recently, by invoking a polymorphous description consisting of large supercells populated with static symmetry-broken motifs whose spatial average restores the paramagnetic state. Inspired by these viewpoints, we introduce the on-site dephased ensemble (DE) approximation, in which the local electronic-structure problem is described by a thermal ensemble of all accessible local static solutions; this gives rise to a strong frequency dependence of the local electronic self-energy, as seen in DMFT or in the coherent-potential approximation of disordered alloys. We show that the DE successfully recovers defining hallmarks of strongly correlated Mott systems, both in terms of the self-energy as well as the persistence of local moments in time, in quantitative agreement with DMFT. By bypassing expensive quantum Monte Carlo solvers or large supercell calculations, this approach offers efficient routes to treating paramagnetic Mott systems in a first-principles setting, and highlights a deeper connection between the physics of strong correlations and that of disorder.
summary: This work introduces the On-site dephased ensemble (DE) approximation to tackle strongly correlated Mott insulators. By averaging over local static solutions, DE efficiently reproduces key signatures of strong correlations seen in DMFT. This offers a powerful, computationally cheaper alternative for studying these challenging electronic systems.
main_problem: The central challenge is accurately solving the many-body electronic structure problem, especially for paramagnetic Mott insulators which defy standard methods like DFT.
main_result: The proposed On-site dephased ensemble (DE) approximation successfully recovers key features of strongly correlated Mott systems, matching DMFT results while offering a computationally efficient first-principles route.
method: The DE approximates the local electronic problem by treating it as a thermal ensemble over all accessible local static solutions, bypassing expensive quantum Monte Carlo or large supercell calculations.
model_or_system: The study focuses on paramagnetic Mott insulators, using models like NiO and FeO within a 5-orbital d-band framework governed by Hubbard interactions (U).
key_observables: Local electronic self-energy ($\Sigma(\omega)$), local spectral function ($A(\omega)$), and the persistence of local moments.
important_parameters: Hubbard interaction strength (e.g., U = 6 eV) and temperature/inverse temperature ($ eta$).
main_assumptions: The DE neglects inter-basin tunneling between static solutions, making it an approximation valid in the limit of strong Hubbard U.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the grand potential landscape of local states, the imaginary part of the self-energy, and the resulting spectral functions for both the ensemble average and individual symmetry-broken states.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the DE approximation by comparing it to DMFT and supercell methods. It then applies this method to paradigmatic Mott insulators (NiO, FeO), benchmarking its results against established DMFT calculations across various observables.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, the concept of describing a complex quantum state as an ensemble average over multiple localized configurations shares conceptual links with open quantum system descriptions and environmental coupling in AMO physics.
